note: Anchors on the DXIL gradient opcode *call site* (`= call ... @dx.op.unary...(i32 83..86, ...)`  -- DerivCoarseX=83/DerivCoarseY=84/DerivFineX=85/DerivFineY=86), not on the op's comment name or the SSA value's textual name. That distinction matters: v1.4.1907 names the defining value itself `%DerivFineX` (old dxc keeps source-derived SSA names), so a later *use* of that already-computed value inside the conditional block (a legitimate, correctly-conditional UAV store of the value) recurs as the substring `DerivFineX` textually after `br i1` even when the call itself was never sunk -- a first version of this predicate matching bare `DerivFineX` false-positived on exactly that. Requiring the `= call ... i32 8[3-6],` idiom only matches an actual derivative *computation*, so the predicate only fires when the compiler regenerates/moves the call itself into the successor block. If the compiler sinks the call (the bug), this idiom appears strictly after the `br i1` that begins the conditional region; if the call stays unconditional (fixed), it appears only before the branch and this pattern does not match. Uses [\s\S] instead of `.` to cross the intervening newlines per this skill's MULTILINE-not-DOTALL note.
